entries.name: GitHub
entries.tagline: Repos, issues, PRs, and Actions in every format agents speak.
entries.description: GitHub exposes more agent-callable surface area than almost any service: an official remote MCP server, a fully-specified REST API, a GraphQL API, and the `gh` CLI. Pick the format that fits your agent — they all reach the same data.

authMethods.label: OAuth 2.0
authMethods.note: The remote MCP server walks compatible clients through OAuth automatically.

authMethods.label: Personal access token
authMethods.note: Fine-grained PATs let you scope access per-repo and per-permission.

entries.name: Google Workspace
entries.tagline: Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Docs, and Sheets from one credential.
entries.description: Google Workspace exposes its services through per-product REST APIs built on the Google Discovery Service, a vendor-published CLI (`gws`), and a popular community CLI (`gog`). All of them authenticate through Google Cloud OAuth — the setup is the hard part, and it's shared across every interface.

authMethods.label: OAuth 2.0 (Desktop client)
authMethods.note: Bring your own Google Cloud project; both CLIs and the APIs use it.

authMethods.label: Service account
authMethods.note: For headless and Workspace-admin scenarios via domain-wide delegation.

entries.name: Linear
entries.tagline: Issues, projects, and cycles — agent-native from day one.
entries.description: Linear's entire product runs on its public GraphQL API, and its hosted MCP server gives agents the same tools the official integrations use: create and update issues, manage projects, and coordinate cycles.

authMethods.label: OAuth 2.0
authMethods.note: Recommended for apps used by others; the MCP server uses it automatically.

authMethods.label: Personal API key
authMethods.note: Best for personal scripts. Sent without a Bearer prefix — a common gotcha.

entries.name: Notion
entries.tagline: Pages, databases, and comments as agent-editable workspace memory.
entries.description: Notion's hosted MCP server lets agents search, create, and reorganize workspace content. The REST API underneath uses internal integrations with explicit page-level sharing — a natural permission boundary for agents.

authMethods.label: OAuth 2.0
authMethods.note: The MCP server and public integrations use OAuth.

authMethods.label: Internal integration secret
authMethods.note: For personal/workspace automations; pages must be explicitly shared with the integration.

entries.name: PostHog
entries.tagline: Product analytics an agent can query in natural language.
entries.description: PostHog's MCP server exposes 50+ tools: run HogQL, build insights and dashboards, manage feature flags. Agents can answer 'what changed in signups last week?' against real product data.

authMethods.label: Personal API key
authMethods.note: Scoped keys created per-use; used by both the MCP server and REST API.

entries.name: Resend
entries.tagline: Send email from any agent with one API key.
entries.description: Resend is an email API built for developers. The official MCP server exposes sending, contacts, audiences, broadcasts, and domain management; the REST API is small enough for an agent to learn in one read.

authMethods.label: API key
authMethods.note: One key, sent as a bearer header. Scoped keys can restrict to sending-only.

entries.name: Sentry
entries.tagline: Errors, traces, and root-cause analysis for debugging agents.
entries.description: Sentry's hosted MCP server gives agents direct access to issues, events, releases, and Seer root-cause runs — the context a coding agent needs to fix what's actually broken in production.

authMethods.label: OAuth 2.0
authMethods.note: The hosted MCP server authenticates via OAuth in supporting clients.

authMethods.label: Auth token
authMethods.note: Organization or personal tokens for the REST API and CI.

entries.name: Shopify
entries.description: Shopify is GraphQL-first: the Admin API for store management and the Storefront API for shopping experiences. Agents authenticate with per-store access tokens from a custom app.

authMethods.label: Admin access token
authMethods.note: Per-store token from a custom app; sent via X-Shopify-Access-Token header.

authMethods.label: Storefront access token
authMethods.note: Public or private token for the Storefront API.

entries.name: Slack
entries.tagline: Read, search, and send messages where your team already works.
entries.description: Slack's hosted MCP server covers messaging, search, and canvases. The underlying Web API is one of the most battle-tested REST surfaces anywhere — token-based, method-oriented, and fully documented.

authMethods.label: OAuth 2.0
authMethods.note: The MCP server and all Slack apps authenticate through OAuth with granular scopes.

authMethods.label: Bot / user token
authMethods.note: Issued after app install; sent as a bearer header to the Web API.

entries.name: Spotify
entries.tagline: Playlists, search, and playback for music-aware agents.
entries.description: Spotify's Web API covers search, playlists, libraries, and playback control. OAuth is mandatory for anything user-specific, with the client-credentials flow available for catalog-only access.

authMethods.label: OAuth 2.0
authMethods.note: Authorization-code flow for user data; client-credentials for catalog-only access.

entries.name: Stripe
entries.tagline: Payments infrastructure with first-class agent tooling.
entries.description: Stripe ships an official MCP server with documentation search and account tools, a meticulously specified REST API, and the Stripe CLI. Restricted API keys make it one of the safest services to hand to an autonomous agent.

authMethods.label: OAuth (MCP)
authMethods.note: Granular, user-based, revocable from the Dashboard. Recommended for MCP clients.

authMethods.label: Restricted API key
authMethods.note: For autonomous agents and non-OAuth clients. Never hand an agent your full secret key.

entries.name: Todoist
entries.tagline: Tasks, projects, and reminders your agent can manage.
entries.description: Todoist is a task manager with a mature developer platform. Agents can create and complete tasks, organize projects, and query filters through the unified v1 REST API or the official hosted MCP server.

authMethods.label: Personal API token
authMethods.note: Best for personal scripts and single-user agents.

authMethods.label: OAuth 2.0
authMethods.note: Required for multi-user apps. Newer apps get expiring access tokens with rotating refresh tokens.

entries.name: Vercel
entries.tagline: Deployments, projects, and logs your agent can ship with.
entries.description: Vercel's official MCP server covers documentation search, project management, and deployment analysis. The REST API and CLI give agents full control of the deploy loop — push, inspect, roll back.

authMethods.label: OAuth 2.0
authMethods.note: The hosted MCP server uses OAuth in supporting clients.

authMethods.label: Access token
authMethods.note: Account tokens for the REST API; scope to a team where possible.
